## Design

### 2026-10-18 – Spent 3 hours designing and finalising the custom two-part enclosure for the handheld cyberdeck in Tinkercad. The top shell was constructed on a 92 mm x 67 mm base plate with a 15mm  thickness, featur

**5h**

Spent 3 hours designing and finalising the custom two-part enclosure for the handheld cyberdeck in Tinkercad. The top shell was constructed on a 92 mm x 67 mm base plate with a 15mm  thickness, featuring precise cutouts for the 2.4" TFT display active window , an 8x8 LED matrix, dual push buttons, and a front rotary encoder cutout designed to hang slightly off the bottom edge for easy thumb control. The matching bottom tray was hollowed out with 2mm walls to house the dual-board stackup and LiPo battery, complete with an  floor cutout for the ESP32 camera lens and a side-wall slot engineered to let a flat disc thumbwheel potentiometer protrude by 6mm for smooth volume control. Both primary components were grouped, verified for clearance tolerances, and prepared as separate STL files ready for 3D printing.

### 2026-10-18 – Continued the CAD session by designing and finalizing the matching bottom tray enclosure to house the internal hardware stackup. A 2mm wall thickness was maintained around a hollow interior cavity siz

**2h**

Continued the CAD session by designing and finalizing the matching bottom tray enclosure to house the internal hardware stackup. A 2mm wall thickness was maintained around a hollow interior cavity sized specifically to fit the dual-board PCB stack, LiPo battery, and power routing. Cut a targeted 8.5mm aperture into the bottom floor to align cleanly with the ESP32 camera module lens, and added a side-wall slot engineered for a flat disc thumbwheel potentiometer to protrude by approximately 6mm for easy volume adjustment. With both top and bottom enclosure pieces fully hollowed, cut out, and verified for assembly fitment, the CAD models were grouped and prepared for individual STL export for 3D printing.
